new.title: TOI-3686: A Hot Jupiter and Sub-Neptune In A 2:1 Mean-Motion Resonance
new.summary: Hot Jupiters are typically thought to be "lonely", but a small and growing subset of them have been found to have nearby planets in the same system. We present the discovery of a new member of this class of systems, TOI-3686. TOI-3686 c is a hot Jupiter with $P_\mathrm{orb} = 5.078$ days detected by NASA's TESS mission that shows peak-to-peak transit timing variations (TTVs) of 40 minutes, amongst the largest ever observed for a hot Jupiter. A subsequent search of the TESS data revealed the transits of a second planet, TOI-3686 b, a sub-Neptune with $P_\mathrm{orb} = 2.54$~days and peak-to-peak TTVs of 10 hours, $\sim 16\%$ of its orbital period. We characterized the system through photodynamical modeling of photometry from TESS and ground-based facilities, as well as radial velocity measurements from the NEID and MAROON-X spectrographs. We find that the two planets in the TOI-3686 system are deep in a 2:1 mean-motion resonance, making this the only hot Jupiter system currently known to be in a truly resonant configuration, which may be related to its $\lesssim1$~Gyr system age. Systems like TOI-3686 likely formed through a dynamically quiescent pathway and were captured into resonance after migration through a disk, and may represent the high-mass end of processes that occur in compact systems of smaller planets.

new.title: A sub-Earth-sized TESS planet candidate in the nearby M-dwarf binary GJ 774, most likely orbiting GJ 774 A (TIC 351339274)
new.summary: Small planets transiting the nearest M dwarfs are the terrestrial planets most accessible to detailed characterisation. We report a sub-Earth-sized transiting planet candidate in the wide (17.6") M-dwarf binary GJ 774 at 12.86 pc, most likely orbiting the M2.5 primary GJ 774 A (TIC 351339274). The signal was a SPOC multi-sector threshold-crossing event (MES = 7.95) and is not a TESS Object of Interest. In eight TESS sectors (2019-2026) a 1.28-h transit recurs every 4.225138 +/- 0.000010 d with a box-mean depth of 365 +/- 32 ppm in A's light. The 2026 data, which entered neither the SPOC search nor our selection, show it at the ephemeris predicted from 2019-2023 data (304 +/- 43 ppm; none of 10^5 phase-scrambled versions of the 2026 data is as deep). The per-target false-alarm probability is < 0.03 at 95%. Odd/even, secondary-eclipse, archival-plate and Gaia radial-velocity tests exclude unrelated blended eclipsing binaries and eclipsing companions on 4.2-d orbits, and hierarchical eclipsing binaries are improbable. The stars are 0.85 TESS pixel apart, so the TRICERATOPS false-positive probability (0.26) is set by a planet on GJ 774 B. B is disfavoured because its own light does not dim enough: PRF-deblended photometry gives 109 +/- 115 ppm in B's light, against 1089 ppm required if B were the host. Conditional on a point source at A or at B, the joint host model gives P(A)=0.59-0.97 (0.97 for the native target-pixel baseline). Over all sectors the PRF photometry is consistent with A, but in the out-of-sample 2026 data 40% of the deficit appears at B's position, an unexplained 2-3 sigma (PSF-model and depth dependent) tension with host A. On A the planet has R_p=0.70 +/- 0.06 R_Earth, S=15.0 +/- 1.8 S_Earth and T_eq=548 +/- 16 K. It is not validated; resolved ground-based photometry of the pair would test host B directly.

new.title: Large fluctuations and cusp-core transformation in dwarf galaxies
new.summary: Dwarf galaxies are abundant and dark matter dominated, rendering them particularly relevant for testing a cosmological model dominated by a dark sector. Whether their density profiles agree with $\Lambda$CDM expectations has long been a point of contention, dubbed the cusp/core problem. While numerical simulations have suggested that the erasure of central dark matter cusps may arise from potential fluctuations in feedback-driven gas, whether the required fluctuation levels are achieved in actual galaxies has remained uncertain. By measuring the power spectra of neutral gas density contrasts in a sample of gas-rich dwarf galaxies, we show that the observed fluctuations match theoretical expectations when their impact is derived from a stochastic dynamical model. Specifically, the relaxation times for core formation at the observationally estimated radii are generally on the order of a Hubble time or less. Core sizes are therefore consistent with conservative estimates assuming their generation through steady fluctuations acting over cosmic history. The relaxation time increases with halo mass, suggesting that core formation via this mechanism becomes less efficient in more massive systems.

new.title: Resolving the extended interstellar medium of infrared galaxies II. Fine-structure line emission
new.summary: We investigate how star formation and active galactic nuclei (AGNs) shape the ionized and neutral interstellar medium in 67 nearby luminous and ultraluminous infrared galaxies from the Great Observatories All-sky LIRG Survey (GOALS). Combining mid-infrared (MIR) spectral mapping from the Spitzer Infrared Spectrograph with far-infrared (FIR) spectroscopy from the Herschel Photodetector Array Camera and Spectrometer, we measure fine-structure emission lines in aperture grids extending to projected galactocentric distances of about 14 kpc. We compare the measurements with CLOUDY photoionization models to constrain the ionization parameter, hydrogen density, stellar age, and metallicity. In starburst-dominated galaxies, the combined MIR+FIR fits yield a decreasing ionization parameter with radius, approximately constant hydrogen densities, uniformly young stellar populations, and flat metallicity profiles. MIR-only fits instead yield an increasing ionization parameter with radius, highlighting the importance of FIR diagnostics, particularly the [C II] emission associated with photodissociation regions, in constraining the multiphase gas. In the strongest AGN-dominated system, the nucleus and inner extended regions show elevated [Ne III]/[Ne II] and suppressed [C II]/[O I] ratios, while the outermost regions, at projected distances of about 6 kpc and beyond, show values typical of star-forming regions. This suggests that the AGN may affect gas excitation out to about 5 kpc. Our results demonstrate the importance of combining MIR and FIR diagnostics to recover radial trends that can be hidden in galaxy-integrated measurements. Together with Paper I, they provide a benchmark for spatially resolved studies of gas and dust in starbursts and AGN-hosting galaxies.

new.title: Resolving the extended interstellar medium of infrared galaxies I. Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon emission
new.summary: We investigate spatial variations in polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) properties and photoelectric heating efficiency in 67 nearby luminous infrared galaxies from the Great Observatories All-sky LIRG Survey (GOALS). Using mid-infrared spectroscopy from Spitzer and far-infrared cooling-line maps from Herschel, we extract spectra in concentric annuli and matched aperture grids out to about 14 kpc. PAH features are measured with the CAFE spectral decomposition tool. We trace photoelectric heating efficiency by combining PAH emission with cooling lines after isolating the neutral-gas contribution. In starburst galaxies, the PAH 11.3/7.7 ratio rises out to about 5 kpc while 6.2/7.7 remains nearly constant, indicating predominantly large, neutral PAHs. Between 5 and 8 kpc, 11.3/7.7 continues to rise while inferred PAH sizes decrease. Beyond 8 kpc, 11.3/7.7 falls and 6.2/7.7 rises, indicating smaller, more ionized PAHs. These trends are consistent with PAH photodestruction near the central starburst. Strong active galactic nucleus (AGN) systems show more neutral PAHs and harder radiation fields in their nuclear and inner regions. Beyond about 5 kpc, PAHs become more ionized and approach the starburst locus as the radiation field weakens. Strong AGNs influence average PAH charge states at 6-14 kpc as effectively as moderate AGNs at 1-6 kpc. Photoelectric heating efficiency increases with radius in both starburst and AGN-hosting galaxies as the radiation field weakens. In starbursts, higher efficiency is associated with more neutral PAHs, while AGN-dominated systems show the opposite relation. These results provide quantitative, spatially resolved constraints on the extent of AGN effects on dust properties in a population of luminous infrared galaxies.

new.title: Automated optimization of solar energetic particle acceleration and transport parameters against five-spacecraft observations of the 9 October 2021 event
new.summary: Solar energetic particle (SEP) events threaten space infrastructure, yet physics-based prediction models depend on numerous poorly constrained free parameters. We introduce the Fujitsu Solar Energetic particle Intelligent Tuning and Evaluation Network (SEITEN), which couples the SUSANOO MHD model of CME propagation to SEPIF, a diffusive shock acceleration and focused transport model, through the shock conditions SUSANOO supplies, and automatically optimizes the free parameters of the particle model against the SEP event of 9 October 2021. The mean free path and the injection efficiency vary independently along each magnetic field line and heliolongitudinal bin, giving a 19-dimensional problem solved by quasi-Monte Carlo sampling followed by a Tree-structured Parzen Estimator. The optimized model reproduces proton flux profiles at five spacecraft with a mean absolute error of $\approx 0.45$ in $\log_{10}$ flux, and the inferred mean free paths show a clear east-west structure; these are effective parameters conditional on the assumed transport geometry. Six independent runs show that whether mean free paths or injection efficiencies dominate depends on the MHD shock strength, and that injection efficiencies differ by orders of magnitude between MHD configurations despite nearly identical fit quality. Joint MHD-SEP parameter estimation is therefore a necessary next step towards generalized, operational SEP forecasting.

new.title: Community Lessons from builders of infrared multi-object spectrographs
new.summary: We present a summary of lessons learned from our community on the design and construction of infrared multi-object spectrographs. As members of the Magellan Infrared Multi-Object Spectrograph (MIRMOS) development team, we were motivated to learn about the most common troubles faced by our colleagues and incorporate measures in our design and assembly plan to address known issues. The lessons are compiled as a result of interviews we carried out with members of the instrument development teams for several multi-object infrared spectrographs. We found considerable overlap in the lessons learned for building this type of instrument; many of which relate to the cryogenic operation of the instruments. In this paper, we will present the compilation of general and specific lessons which we found relevant for the successful development of MIRMOS or any other future cryogenic instruments.

new.title: Slow-Roll Inflation at Arbitrary Order
new.summary: We derive explicit expressions for the primordial scalar and tensor spectra at arbitrary finite order $p$ in the slow-roll expansion, valid both for canonical single-field inflation and $k$-inflation. At any order, the spectra are determined by known combinations of slow-roll parameters weighted by universal coefficients entirely fixed by the free de Sitter solutions, without requiring perturbatively corrected mode functions. Using these spectra, we obtain closed-form consistency relations that connect the tensor tilt $n_t$ and its runnings $\alpha_n^t\equiv d^n n_t/d(\ln k)^n$ to the tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$, the scalar spectral index $n_s$, and its runnings $\alpha_n^s\equiv d^n(n_s-1)/d(\ln k)^n$. The consistency relations are valid for arbitrary $n\geq 0$ and any finite $p\geq 0$, without recursion over lower-order relations. For $k$-inflation, they additionally depend on the scalar sound speed and its scale derivatives. We develop an algorithm that generates both the spectra and consistency relations for any pair $(n,p)$. We reproduce known results through next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order (N3LO) and extend the explicit calculations up to N10LO.

new.title: Dynamical stability of Magnetic Supramassive Neutron Stars
new.summary: We investigate the dynamical stability of strongly magnetized supramassive neutron stars close to the mass-shedding limit using fully general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamic simulations in three spatial dimensions. Equilibrium configurations are constructed using a microphysical equation of state and considering poloidal magnetic fields up to maximum strengths ${\sim} 10^{17}\,\mathrm{G}$. The initially unstable magnetic fields reorganize into mixed poloidal--toroidal configurations on Alfvén timescales shorter than the stellar rotation period. The subsequent dynamical evolution is governed by timescales set by the Lehnert number. For stars with masses sufficiently lower than the maximum mass, magnetic stresses redistribute angular momentum and drive the development of differential rotation, leading to a new quasi-stationary configuration that remains dynamically stable over several rotation periods. Magnetically-driven winds develop from the outer layers around the equatorial plane and remain baryon-matter dominated with magnetization ${\lesssim}0.2$. Over the simulated timescale, winds carry a total rest mass of order ${\sim}10^{-3}\mathrm{M}_\odot$ at outflow rates of up to a few $M_\odot/\mathrm{s}$. For stars close to (or beyond) the maximum-mass turning point along the stellar equilibrium sequence, strong magnetic fields trigger gravitational collapse by redistributing angular momentum away from the stellar core. The resulting black hole remnants are characterized by angular velocities up to ${\sim}49\%$ larger and angular momentum ${\lesssim}8\%$ smaller than those of the initial equilibrium stars. Our results show that extreme magnetic-field instabilities can significantly alter the structure of supramassive neutron stars, with possible implications for magnetars and long-lived binary neutron-star merger remnants.

new.title: Constraints on Millimeter-wave Extragalactic Transient Populations from 4 Years of SPT-3G data
new.summary: Wide-field cosmic microwave background (CMB) instruments have reached sufficient sensitivity and cadence to conduct untargeted millimeter-wave searches for astronomical transients. To date, such searches have primarily discovered stellar flares, while extragalactic detections remain limited to a few flaring blazars and active galactic nuclei. In contrast, recent simulations suggest that current and future CMB experiments should detect a few to dozens of extragalactic transients per year from sources including gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), tidal disruption events, and fast blue optical transients. At timescales under one week, predicted detections are dominated by flares from reverse shocks in long-duration GRBs, with some benchmark models predicting rates of ~10 detections per year for the SPT-3G camera on the South Pole Telescope. In this work, we conduct a transient search optimized for the bright and brief millimeter-wave emission from GRB reverse shocks. We update previous simulations by incorporating a more realistic model of the SPT-3G sensitivity, observing cadence, and detection algorithm, resulting in nearly a factor of two improvement in detection sensitivity compared to prior estimates. We subsequently carry out a search over four seasons of the 1500 deg2 SPT-3G Main field observations from 2019-22, finding no candidate extragalactic events. We use the lack of detections to constrain the parameters of the synthesized GRB populations, setting upper limits on the fraction of GRBs with reverse shock components, f_RS, and the all-sky rate of reverse shocks beamed at Earth, N_all-sky. For a standard 10^51 erg GRB with Lorentz factor Gamma = 100, we constrain f_RS <0.57 and N_all-sky <1226 bursts/year (at 90% confidence). The most readily detectable model we consider is a 10^52 erg "dirty" GRB with Gamma = 50, whose population we constrain to f_RS <0.09 and N_all-sky <120 bursts/year.

cross.title: Searching for axions with quantum interferometry
cross.summary: Quantum phase measurements offer a complementary route to axion searches. We show that axion-photon interactions can imprint both Aharonov-Bohm (AB) and Berry phases in experimentally motivated quantum setups. For a coherently oscillating axion dark matter background, the induced effective current generates a time dependent magnetic flux in an rf-SQUID, leading to a measurable voltage signal through the Josephson phase. For representative benchmarks, this AB phase search reaches the minimum axion-photon coupling $g_{a\gamma\gamma}^{\mathrm{min}}\sim 7.8\times10^{-14}~\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$ at axion mass $m_a\sim 10^{-10}~\mathrm{eV}$, with projected sensitivity that can improve on existing limits in that parameter space by roughly one to two orders of magnitude. We also identify a geometric phase observable in a Mach-Zehnder interferometer with an adiabatically rotating magnetic field, providing a proof-of-principle phase-based probe of meV-scale axions even when they do not constitute the dark matter, although sensitivity on the coupling remains weaker than current bounds with conservative tabletop benchmarks. Extending the analysis to a three level photon-axion quasiparticle (AQP)-axion system, with the AQP realized in a topological magnetic insulator, we find a potentially measurable THz Berry phase dominated by the AQP sector, furnishing a nontrivial validation of the formalism in a richer coupled system. These setups establish quantum phase observables as a useful new framework for axion searches, with immediate phenomenological promise in superconducting circuits and longer term potential in quantum enhanced interferometry.

cross.title: Search for Compact Binary Coalescences with Sub-solar Mass Components in Data from the Second Part of LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA's Fourth Observing Run
cross.summary: We report on a gravitational wave search for compact binary coalescences with secondary mass between 0.2 M and 1 M and primary mass between 0.2 M and 10 M, restricting the component mass ratio to lie between 0.1 and 1. The analysis uses data collected by the LIGO and Virgo detectors between 2024 April 10 15:00:00 and 2025 January 28 17:00:00, the second part of the fourth observing run of the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA Collaboration. Results from two out of three search pipelines show outlier candidates, but not at a sufficient level of significance to provide evidence for detection. We report the combined sensitivity of the current searches over the first and second parts of the observing run to the target sub-solar mass (SSM) black hole (BH) population, as well as to neutron star (NS) binaries with one or more sub-solar component. We place upper limits on the merger rate of SSM BHs, ranging from $50 {\rm Gpc}^{-3} {\rm yr}^{-1}$ to~$5000 {\rm Gpc}^{-3} {\rm yr}^{-1}$ (90% confidence) for different component mass combinations. We use the merger rate limits to constrain two illustrative dark matter (DM) scenarios that can form SSM compact objects: primordial BHs, and dark BHs forming in a dissipative DM model. Our search limits the fraction of DM in primordial BHs, assuming a monochromatic mass distribution, to be $\leq$ (0.018-0.032) at 1 M, and $\leq$ (0.10-0.18) at 0.35 M for early-forming binaries; or to be less than 1 at masses above (0.62-0.74) M for late-forming binaries. For the dissipative model, we constrain the fraction of DM for a range of minimum dark black hole masses below $1\,M$ to be as low as (1.0-1.1) x $10^{-5}$; we also exclude minimum masses above (0.62-0.74) M, if dark BHs constitute all of the DM. For binary NSs that include sub-solar mass components, assuming a simple, fixed population model we find a merger rate upper limit of $249 {\rm Gpc}^{-3} {\rm yr}^{-1}$.

cross.title: Adaptive Model-Switch Thermodynamic Integration: A Bayes Factor Estimator
cross.summary: Bayes factors are a widely used model comparison criterion, but are often quite challenging and computationally expensive to estimate well. We propose a variation of the model-switch thermodynamic integration method for estimating Bayes factors that decreases the variance of the estimator and essentially eliminates integration error. We choose samples whose density in $\beta$ is proportional to the standard deviation of previously drawn samples. Rather than averaging many samples at each $\beta$, we use a very dense set of $\beta$ values, collecting one sample at each in order of increasing $\beta$ and one sample at each in order of decreasing $\beta$ to minimize "thermic lag". We study our procedure with a toy model (based loosely on some signal recovery problems). In this model we find that adaptive sampling gives us a 2.7-fold decrease in the spread of the estimated Bayes factor. We test our procedure both drawing directly from the posterior distribution and using a Markov Chain Monte Carlo sampler.

cross.title: Ion Heating in Pair-loaded Relativistic Turbulence
cross.summary: Pair-loaded relativistic turbulence is expected in compact high-energy astrophysical environments and may sustain plasma heating. Using self-consistent three-dimensional radiative particle-in-cell simulations, we identify the mechanism of ion heating mediated by pair-enhanced radiative feedback in relativistic turbulence. We derive the theoretical criterion for the transition to a regime dominated by radiative feedback and show that pair loading promotes the growth and persistence of large, connected optically thick structures. These long-lived structures sustain intense localized ion heating, repeatedly generating prominent hot-ion clumps and substantially enhancing the mean ion temperature. Our results establish a physical link between pair creation and sustained ion heating, providing a theoretical basis for investigating intermittent hot-ion production in black-hole coronae and gamma-ray burst outflows.

cross.title: Floquet Instability of Photon-Axion Conversion
cross.summary: The discovery of axions would provide evidence for physics beyond the Standard Model. In this work, we investigate axion-photon conversion in the presence of a background magnetic field with simultaneous spatial and temporal periodicity. By performing a Lorentz transformation, the coupled axion-photon system is mapped onto a time-periodic linear system that can be analyzed using Floquet theorem. We find unstable modes associated with resonant crossing between Floquet replicas. The resulting complex Floquet exponents lead to exponentially growing modes, which we identify as a Floquet instability. Then, we determine the parameter regions in which this instability appears in a perturbative analysis. We further show that the Floquet instability enhances the axion-field amplitude generated from an initial photon field. Our results demonstrate that spatiotemporally periodic magnetic backgrounds provide a distinct mechanism for modifying axion-photon conversion through Floquet instability.

cross.title: Elementary-Symmetric Ricci Gravity: Metric Formulation
cross.summary: We investigate a four-dimensional metric theory of gravity whose Lagrangian is a linear combination of the elementary symmetric polynomials of the Ricci tensor. We derive the field equations and characterize Einstein vacua and a real, diagonalizable class of parallel-Ricci vacua. The latter includes direct products of two constant-curvature surfaces and can exhibit a hierarchy of curvature radii. The Einstein vacua possess multiple branches associated with the distinct roots of a polynomial, whose multiple roots define boundaries in parameter space. We derive the linearized equations on maximally symmetric backgrounds, distinguish the scalar and spin-2 degrees of freedom, and then analyze their classical linear stability. We also obtain the generalized Friedmann constraint and the associated homogeneous evolution equations. An illustrative spatially flat solution evolves from the neighborhood of an unstable de Sitter solution toward a stable de Sitter solution. This behavior may motivate further investigation into early- and late-time accelerated expansion and provide a gravity-driven mechanism for automatic end of inflation.

cross.title: Annihilation feedback on elastic scattering in self-interacting dark matter
cross.summary: Sizable dark-matter self-interactions, motivated by observations of galactic structure, often arise from the exchange of light force mediators. Light mediators can render scattering nonperturbative and make inelastic processes important. Unitarity, via the optical theorem, implies that elastic and inelastic interactions cannot be treated independently: inelasticity induces absorptive contributions to the two-particle self-energy kernel that determines the elastic amplitude, while the resulting incoming-state dynamics also modifies the inelastic amplitudes. We study the feedback of dark-matter annihilation on elastic scattering in the presence of a long-range force. Although annihilation is a short-distance process, it can be strongly enhanced by such a force. We find that its feedback becomes significant near Sommerfeld resonances, where it suppresses the low-velocity growth of the baseline elastic cross section. Near baseline elastic-scattering zeros, it may instead generate a nonzero elastic floor required by unitarity. A companion paper studies the feedback of radiative bound-state formation on elastic scattering, which can generate sizable self-interactions.

cross.title: A Natural Dark Matter-Dark Energy Interaction from Axion-Monopole Dynamics
cross.summary: We propose a natural framework for interacting dark matter and dark energy based on axion-monopole dynamics in a dark gauge sector. Dark matter is composed of dark 't Hooft-Polyakov monopoles, while dark energy is an ultralight axion whose coupling to the dark gauge field induces an axion-dependent dyon mass through the Witten effect. This generates a direct dark matter-dark energy interaction. We show that generic models with a significant dark matter-dark energy coupling suffer from a naturalness problem: the Coleman-Weinberg potential induced by the interaction is typically much larger than the dark energy scale. In our model, the corrections arise from a monodromy tower of dyon states, allowing them to be exponentially suppressed. In the minimal setup, the interaction strength is predicted to be $\sim 0.1\%$, below the sensitivity of current observations. We discuss scenarios in which cosmological population of higher-charge dyons can enhance the interaction to the percent level, producing an apparent phantom dark energy equation of state. We further show that the parameter space of the axion-monopole model preferred by fitting the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) results can also naturally explain the cosmic birefringence with a small anomaly coefficient.

cross.title: Deglobalising the fit: how to search for physics beyond vacuum General Relativity in LISA catalogues
cross.summary: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna will observe up to $\sim 10^{7}$ overlapping signals, which have to be characterised simultaneously with a global fit. This is a challenge for model comparison since rerunning the global fit for every physical model of interest, including deviations from vacuum General Relativity, is computationally demanding. An alternative is a two-step post-processing strategy: a first global fit with vacuum models only, after which a selected group of target sources is reanalysed under a different model with all other sources subtracted. We show that in this strategy a beyond-vacuum effect in a target source can be partly absorbed by the overlapping nuisance sources in the first fit, subtracted with them, and never reach the reanalysis. In the linear-signal approximation, the loss is captured by a single number, the masking ratio $\mathcal{R}\in[0,1]$. A deviation the global fit would detect at $n_\sigma$ is reported by post-processing at $\mathcal{R}\,n_\sigma$, and bounds in null tests are also reported too tight by the same factor. We show how to compute $\mathcal{R}$ from the posterior samples of the vacuum global fit, and give an algorithm that ranks the nuisance sources by how much of the effect each can absorb, so that only those most correlated with it need to be refitted with the target in a down-scaled reanalysis with a few sources. We validate our method with full Markov-chain Monte Carlo inference on a toy model of 21 overlapping chirping sinusoids, where one carries a small non-linear chirp that represents the missed physics, while the other 20 act as nuisance sources. This method can serve as a basis for tests of General Relativity in realistic LISA mock datasets and can be adapted to study the impact of systematics between different gravitational-wave sources.

cross.title: Cosmic birefringence from a stiff axion field and its cosmological implications
cross.summary: We propose a model in which the observed cosmic microwave background birefringence arises from the interaction of photons with a stiff ($w=1$) pseudo-scalar field that today contributes a subdominant fraction of the total energy density, distinct from both dark matter and dark energy. Big Bang Nucleosynthesis constrains the cosmological density of the stiff field, leading to a lower bound for its coupling with photons, $g_{\phi\gamma} > 8.9 \times 10^{-14}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$. Photon conversion in cluster-hosted quasars sets an upper bound, $g_{\phi\gamma} < 5.0 \times 10^{-13}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$. Therefore, there is a narrow window for the discovery of this cosmological component that can be explored in the forthcoming years with astrophysical axion searches. Moreover, we show that this scenario leads to gravitational-wave signals that can be tested with planned experiments.

cross.title: Modular Bayesian Inference for Partially Misspecified Mixtures with Uncertain Class Labels
cross.summary: Scientific inference often involves observations from multiple latent populations whose class memberships are uncertain and must be inferred from available data. While full Bayesian mixture modelling provides a principled approach to joint uncertainty quantification in this setting, often the model is misspecified or less trustworthy for populations that are not the target of the inference, which can distort posterior inference for the parameters of interest. We propose a modular Bayesian framework that safeguards against such biases. We decouple classification from downstream inference using fixed class probabilities, for example from a classifier trained on a subset of labelled data. We then protect inference on the parameters of interest by preventing the likelihood contributions of less trustworthy populations from influencing them. A key benefit of this principled modularization is that it greatly simplifies inference, reducing a fully joint mixture analysis to sampling label allocations, fitting the protected downstream model for each sample, and averaging the resulting posteriors. We establish calibration conditions on these class probabilities under which the proposed procedure preserves the inferential target of the analysis with known labels, and demonstrate the method in synthetic experiments and in cosmological analysis of photometric supernova samples.

cross.title: Self-interacting dark matter from radiative bound-state-formation feedback
cross.summary: Observations of galactic structure motivate sizable dark-matter self-interactions at low velocities, naturally realized through light force mediators. Such mediators can also make inelastic processes very efficient. Unitarity then requires their absorptive contributions to the two-particle self-energy kernel to be resummed, which in turn feeds back into both the elastic and inelastic scattering amplitudes. We study the feedback of radiative bound-state formation on elastic scattering and its implications for self-interacting dark matter. We focus on capture processes through emission of a charged scalar; such transitions are particularly efficient because the scattering and bound states are governed by different effective potentials, a feature also shared by radiative capture through emission of a non-Abelian gauge boson. We show that their feedback can generate sizable elastic scattering relevant for halo dynamics, even when the baseline elastic amplitude vanishes. Notably, the generated elastic cross section can grow toward low velocities, resembling long-range scattering. A companion paper examines the feedback from annihilation processes.

cross.title: Illuminating Light Dark Matter with Fixed-Target Experiments
cross.summary: Astronomical and cosmological observations provide overwhelming evidence for a non-luminous matter component, dark matter (DM), whose particle nature remains unknown. Experimental searches for non-gravitational DM interactions have largely targeted DM with GeV-TeV masses via nuclear recoils, yielding no discovery thus far. DM in the MeV-GeV mass range, however, is theoretically motivated, reproducing the observed relic abundance while remaining invisible to nuclear recoil searches. Such light DM is better probed via electron recoils or at fixed-target experiments. This thesis advances the theoretical and statistical toolkit for light DM searches at fixed-target experiments, spanning model building, statistical inference, global fits, and signal simulation. We survey the landscape of fixed-target searches for light DM, focusing on the Light Dark Matter eXperiment (LDMX). We also simulate DM signatures at the next-generation experiment SHiP to assess its sensitivity. Within minimal DM models, we present a likelihood-based statistical framework for LDMX using the full two-dimensional recoil electron distribution, spanning exclusion, discovery, parameter estimation, and model comparison in frequentist and Bayesian formulations. This establishes the discovery potential of LDMX, and we quantify the direct detection exposure needed to independently confirm a potential signal. Beyond this paradigm, we perform global fits of scalar and fermionic light DM, combining cosmological, astrophysical, and laboratory constraints. We then extend fixed-target searches to spin-1 DM and higher electromagnetic moment dark photons, yielding rich signatures with strong complementarity to other probes. Finally, we go beyond standard nuclear modelling of dark photon production, incorporating elastic nuclear form factors and spectral functions from many-body ab initio methods in place of analytic treatments.

cross.title: A Multipole Technique for the Simulation and Analysis of Gravitational Waveforms from Extreme Mass Ratio Inspirals
cross.summary: We introduce EMRICode, a Python-based numerical framework for evolving generic extreme mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) in Kerr spacetime. The code combines adaptive numerical integration of test-particle geodesics with a prescribed model for the secular evolution of the orbital constants of motion, allowing eccentric and inclined trajectories to be followed over long inspiral timescales. We focus in particular on the treatment of the Carter constant, whose evolution is not directly determined by the leading-order fluxes for energy and axial angular momentum used in the present model. We investigate several prescriptions for determining its evolution and find that a radial-potential-based prescription provides the most stable behavior among those considered, while also exhibiting a systematic residual bias for nearly planar orbits. We compare the resulting inspirals with established radiation-reaction approximations, including the weak-field treatment of Peters and Kerr-based prescriptions from the literature, and use these comparisons to assess the qualitative behavior and limitations of the implementation. The modular structure of EMRICode allows the radiation-reaction prescription to be replaced independently of the underlying geodesic evolution, providing a framework for incorporating more accurate flux models and additional physical effects. We present two simple examples of how interactions with accretion disks and partial tidal disruptions can drive the evolution of a stellar EMRI orbit. EMRICode therefore provides a flexible computational framework for studying the orbital dynamics of EMRIs and for exploring extensions beyond the idealized vacuum, point-particle approximation.

cross.title: High-cadence GW astrometry in the $μ$Hz gap
cross.summary: We forecast the sensitivity of a dedicated, fast-spinning astrometric survey to a stochastic gravitational-wave background (SGWB) in the microhertz gap between pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) and LISA. Spinning the satellite faster samples each star more often, raising the Nyquist frequency and opening higher frequencies at no cost in noise: the shorter, noisier exposures are exactly compensated by their number, so the white-noise floor of each position stream is independent of cadence. High frequencies are where astrometry is most competitive, because the deflection measures the strain directly: its strain noise is white, whereas the equivalent noise of pulsar timing grows as $f^2$. With a cross-correlation estimator over $N$ reference stars and the astrometric overlap computed in the distant-source limit, we find that a Gaia-like satellite scanning the ecliptic poles, with $N\sim10^4$ bright stars over $10$~yr, falls short of the background measured by PTAs by a factor $\sim\!60$. A larger, $8$-m-class aperture, or a constellation of satellites covering the whole sky, reaches it, while extending the reach continuously across the $\mu$Hz band.

cross.title: P-ONE-1: the first detector line of the Pacific Ocean Neutrino Experiment
cross.summary: Neutrino telescopes instrument optically transparent media with three-dimensional arrays of photosensors to detect Cherenkov radiation induced by neutrino interactions within or near the instrumented volume. The small cross-sections of the weak interaction and the low neutrino fluxes above TeV energies require vast detector volumes, which only natural media on Earth can realistically provide. Spurred by the detection of the first neutrino sources by the IceCube Neutrino Observatory, a new generation of neutrino telescopes is emerging to increase the global instrumented volume and detection sensitivity. The Pacific Ocean Neutrino Experiment (P-ONE) aims to install such a telescope in the Northeast Pacific Ocean, building on established neutrino telescope design targets in collaboration with Ocean Networks Canada (ONC). This article presents the design, integration, and testing of the first P-ONE line, P-ONE-1, in preparation for its deployment and integration into ONC's deep-sea observatory NEPTUNE. Alongside the detector design and integration methods, we detail in-air and in-water system-level validation performed at several test sites in Canada, culminating in the successful construction of P-ONE-1 and its preparation for deployment.

cross.title: Stability Analysis of Axion Dark Energy Model
cross.summary: We investigate the stability of an axion dark energy model characterized by a periodic scalar-field potential motivated by pseudo Nambu Goldstone bosons. While such models are well suited to drive late-time cosmic acceleration and can exhibit rich dynamical features, including oscillatory behavior of the dark-energy equation-of-state parameter, their viability crucially depends on the existence of stable cosmological solutions. By reformulating the background evolution equations as an autonomous dynamical system, we identify the fixed points corresponding to radiation-dominated, matter-dominated, and dark energy dominated epochs. Using both analytical and numerical techniques, we analyze the stability properties of these fixed points within the observationally allowed region of parameter space. Our results show that the radiation- and matter-dominated phases emerge naturally as saddle points, ensuring a standard cosmological evolution, while the late-time dark energy dominated solution acts as a stable attractor. This guarantees the robustness of cosmic acceleration against variations in initial conditions. Overall, our study establishes the axion dark energy model as a dynamically consistent and observationally viable candidate for explaining the late-time accelerated expansion of the Universe.

cross.title: Untangling Extreme Mass Ratio Inspirals and Massive Black Hole Binaries in LISA Data
cross.summary: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will observe sources in the millihertz regime, such as Galactic Binaries (GBs), Massive Black Hole Binaries (MBHBs), and Extreme Mass Ratio Inspirals (EMRIs), so its data stream will be a superposition of an unknown number of gravitational-wave sources. We consider the joint inference of various representative combinations of MBHB and EMRI signals in LISA data (with assumed instrumental noise and stochastic GB foreground). Our Bayesian analyses confirm the expectation of weak inter-source coupling between EMRIs, and between EMRIs and MBHBs, despite strong intra-source parameter correlations. Weak EMRI-MBHB coupling enables a hierarchically sequential approach to EMRI and MBHB inference, rather than fully joint inference. We further show that imperfect MBHB subtraction, arising from missing modes or overlapping MBHBs, has only a weak impact on EMRI inference. For multiple MBHBs, we mitigate inference errors through a joint MBHB fit. We demonstrate this strategy on simulated LISA data containing noise, three MBHBs, and three EMRIs, jointly fitting and subtracting the MBHBs before sequentially inferring the EMRIs - ultimately observing little to no bias on all recovered astrophysical parameters. The notions described throughout our work are highly relevant to informing optimal strategies for the global-fit-based pipelines that are currently being developed for LISA.

cross.title: Axion detection in the non-Markovian noise
cross.summary: The detection of axion dark matter poses a significant challenge due to its exceptionally weak coupling to standard-model particles. Here we develop a noise-tolerant quantum-metrology scheme based on coupled $^{129}$Xe spin ensembles to search for such weakly interacting particles. Within an experimentally accessible parameter regime, our scheme achieves an ideal exclusion limit on the axion coupling constant that is several orders of magnitude more stringent than that of conventional detection methods. We further investigate the performance of our scheme under dissipative noise and find that its robustness is fundamentally governed by the energy-spectrum structure of the composite spin-environment system. Remarkably, when a bound state emerges in the spectrum, the exclusion limit asymptotically recovers its ideal value in the non-Markovian dynamics, whereas under the Markovian approximation the limit deteriorates significantly due to noise. Our results establish a universal mechanism for noise-resilient exploration of beyond-standard-model physics, which can be practically implemented by engineering bound-state formation via tuning the Larmor frequency of the spin ensembles.

cross.title: Two-Component Dark Matter and Strongly First-Order Electroweak Phase Transition via a Two-Step Mechanism in the Inert Doublet plus Real Singlet Model
cross.summary: We study a two-component dark matter model in which a real singlet scalar and an inert doublet scalar are simultaneously present alongside the Standard Model, each stabilized by an independent discrete symmetry. The real singlet undergoes a strong first-order transition at high temperature, establishing an intermediate phase with a non-zero singlet vacuum expectation value, which in turn generates the barrier required for the Higgs field to complete a strongly first-order electroweak transition at a lower temperature. This two-step mechanism naturally enforces the condition $v_c/T_c \geq 1$, the sphaleron washout-avoidance criterion necessary for electroweak baryogenesis. The gravitational wave spectrum from both steps is computed; the second step produces a decihertz signal, peaking near $0.08$--$0.34~\mathrm{Hz}$ across the viable parameter space and $0.14$--$0.22~\mathrm{Hz}$ at the benchmark points, that reaches the sensitivity of DECIGO for the strongest transitions and of BBO more widely, while the first remains sub-threshold for all planned detectors. At the coupling values required to drive the phase transition, the singlet is generically underabundant as a thermal relic, so the inert doublet carries the dominant fraction of the observed relic density. Confronting the model with current constraints, we find that the LUX-ZEPLIN 2024 result excludes the entire electroweak-phase-transition-viable parameter space of the singlet sector across the full mass range, even after rescaling by the singlet relic fraction, establishing a complete no-go for the singlet as a viable thermal dark matter candidate in this framework.

cross.title: Direct Urca process facilitated by non-Fermi-liquid quantum criticality
cross.summary: Conventional Fermi-liquid theories of dense nuclear matter predict that the direct Urca process requires a proton fraction above a threshold of $Y_p \approx 0.11$--$0.15$, which is rarely reached in low-mass neutron stars. Here we show that this stringent kinematic constraint is drastically relaxed by the non-Fermi liquid behavior arising from superfluid and superconducting quantum criticality in neutron stars. In the non-Fermi-liquid regimes, nucleons have a smooth momentum occupation without a sharp Fermi surface, and their chemical potentials develop a logarithmic temperature dependence. These intrinsic features fundamentally alter the standard $\beta$-equilibrium relation. Consequently, direct Urca neutrino emission can be activated even at low nuclear densities. This modifies the long-standing Urca-threshold paradigm and indicates that direct Urca process has the opportunity to occur in low-mass neutron stars.

cross.title: On the Stability of Tolman Oppenheimer Volkoff Fireholes
cross.summary: We investigate the radial stability of singular Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff fireholes with a radiation equation of state. These configurations contain a naked, negative point-mass singularity surrounded by a positive-density fluid, whose mass profile develops a Schwarzschild-like plateau before approaching an extended, self-similar atmosphere. Using the Prüfer phase method to identify the fundamental radial mode, we consider two outer boundary conditions: vanishing Lagrangian pressure perturbation (open firehole) and vanishing radial displacement (boxed firehole). For both, the fundamental squared frequency changes from positive to negative as the outer boundary exceeds a critical radius $R_c$. We find that $R_c$ follows approximately the same scaling with the central mass parameter as the equilibrium firehole radius $R$. However, the stability thresholds differ significantly: $R_c^{\rm O}<R$ for the open firehole, whereas $R_c^{\rm B}\simeq R$ for the boxed one. The regular zero mode is the derivative of the equilibrium family with respect to the inner lapse normalization at fixed central mass. This gives the boxed threshold a turning-point interpretation and, together with a scaling symmetry of the TOV equations, implies $R_c^{\rm B}\to R$ in the limit of large central mass. Variational bounds show that the rigid wall is the most stabilizing separated, self-adjoint outer boundary condition and that the unbounded configuration is unstable. Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff fireholes are therefore radially unstable unless confined within approximately their firehole radius.

cross.title: Hybrid Stars with Different Amount of Quark Matter
cross.summary: In a previous work, we explored the possibility of neutron stars with large quark cores. Through Bayesian inference, we obtained large sets of equations of state imposing constraints regarding the properties of nuclear matter, mass-radius data from NICER, the GW170817 data from Virgo-LIGO collaboration, perturbative QCD and causality. We also imposed that the maximum mass neutron star (NS$\text{max}$) must have a large quark core. In this work, we obtain a new set of equations of state (SmallQ set) with the same constraints as before. However, we relaxed the last constraint, imposing only that NS$\text{max}$ must have quark core, regardless of its size. We compare the results with the set from our previous paper constrained by NICER and GW170817 observations NJL-GW. For both sets, we use the Relativistic Mean Field model with nonlinear meson interactions for the hadron phase and the Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model with four- and eight-quark interaction terms for the quark phase. The SmallQ set has higher values of phase transition density, with 3 -- 4.5 $\rho_0$, compared to the NJL-GW, with 2 -- 2.5 $\rho_0$. The new set describes NSs with smaller radius and smaller tidal deformability, and is more compatible with NICER and GW170817 data. A difference in the quark matter composition is observed, with a larger quark strange fraction occurring in the SmallQ set. Within this set, $2 M_\odot$ NSs may contain little to no quark matter. It is shown that there is a non negligible fraction of EOS whose mass-radius curve presents a positive slope for 1.8 $M_\odot$ stars, while for nucleonic stars this fraction is negligible and for hyperonic stars the slope is always negative.

cross.title: Exponential Growth of Turbulent Cross Helicity in Shear-Flow-Driven Turbulence
cross.summary: Cross helicity, the velocity--magnetic-field correlation, is an ideal invariant of incompressible magnetohydrodynamics and constrains energy cascades and magnetic-field generation. Although cross helicity typically decays via visco-resistive effects, we analytically demonstrate that it grows exponentially in sheared inhomogeneous turbulence. This cross-helical shear instability is confirmed using three-dimensional numerical simulations. Growth requires a nonzero gradient of the Reynolds--Maxwell stress to produce turbulent cross helicity; this production overcomes effective losses when shear exceeds a threshold set by the ratio of turbulent magnetic to momentum diffusivities.

cross.title: MadStree: automated evaluation of tree-level de Sitter correlators
cross.summary: We first derived the formulae of recursive reduction and dlog-form differential equations for arbitrary tree-level cosmological correlator, taking the external relations of massless bulk propagators into consideration. The differential equations could be systematically solved and provide the efficient evaluation of them. We have implemented this methodology as a user-friendly Mathematica package MadStree for computing arbitrary tree-level cosmological correlators.

repl.title: Lagrangian perturbation theory for modified gravity
repl.summary: We present a formalism to compute Lagrangian displacement fields for a wide range of cosmologies in the context of perturbation theory up to third order. We emphasize the case of theories with scale dependent gravitational strengths, such as chameleons, but our formalism can be accommodated to other modified gravity theories. In the non-linear regime two qualitative features arise. One, as is well known, is that nonlinearities lead to a screening of the force mediated by the scalar field. The second is a consequence of the transformation of the Klein-Gordon equation from Eulerian to Lagrangian coordinates, producing frame-lagging terms that are important especially at large scales, and if not considered, the theory does not reduce to the $\Lambda$CDM model in that limit. We apply our formalism to compute the 1-loop power spectrum and the correlation function in $f(R)$ gravity by using different resummation schemes. We further discuss the IR divergences of these formalisms.

repl.title: Don't miss the forest for the trees: the Lyman alpha forest power spectrum in effective field theory
repl.summary: We derive an effective field theory (EFT) for cosmological Lyman alpha forest fluctuations valid for the power spectrum at the one-loop order. The ``bottom-up'' EFT expansion at the level of the transmitted flux is identical to the line-of-sight dependent bias model first derived by Desjacques et al. We confirm this result by a ``top-down'' derivation based on the exponential map of the optical depth field. Specifically, we show that the combination of the exponential map and conditions of renormalizability generates the same EFT expansion as the ``bottom-up'' approach. In passing, we point out inconsistencies of the tree-level perturbative expansion of the exponential map without counterterms. To facilitate practical applications, we generalize the FFTLog method for efficient calculations of one-loop integrals from new line-of-sight dependent operators. Finally, we compare the one-loop EFT model against data from the Sherwood hydrodynamic simulation. The theory fits the data with sub percent accuracy up to $k= $ 3 $h$Mpc$^{-1}$ at $z= 2.8$ for both 3D and 1D correlations. Our model can be readily used for cosmological full-shape analyses of Lyman alpha forest data.

repl.title: Unveiling dark forces with measurements of the Large Scale Structure of the Universe
repl.summary: Cosmology offers opportunities to test Dark Matter independently of its interactions with the Standard Model. We study the imprints of long-range forces acting solely in the dark sector on the distribution of galaxies, the so-called Large Scale Structure (LSS). We derive the strongest constraint on such forces from a combination of Planck and BOSS data. Along the way we consistently develop, for the first time, the Effective Field Theory of LSS in the presence of new dynamics in the dark sector. We forecast that future surveys will improve the current bound by an order of magnitude.

repl.title: Causality and perturbative-QCD constraints on first-order phase transitions in neutron stars
repl.summary: Causality bounds the compactness and maximum mass of neutron stars. We generalise this bound to equations of state (EOSs) with a first-order phase transition between maximally stiff phases. In units of the transition energy density, the problem depends only on $q=\ptr/\etr$ and $j=\Delta\ve/\etr$. The maximum compactness equals the smooth value $\mathcal{C}=0.354$ for $q\to0$ or $j\to0$, is unaffected for $q\gtrsim0.67$, and is otherwise reduced by typically $\lesssim0.04$ when the maximum-mass star is a hybrid star and by up to $0.13$ when it is the last hadronic star. Matching to a Baym--Pethick--Sutherland crust and a chiral-EFT polytrope at $n_m=1.1\,n_0$ and inverting the bound, no causal EOS supports $2.01\,\Msun$ if the energy-density jump exceeds $\simeq460$--$495~{\rm MeV\,fm^{-3}}$. Additionally, imposing radius constraint of $R\ge11.6$~km it shrinks to $\simeq235$--$395~{\rm MeV\,fm^{-3}}$. These limits hold whatever the matter above the transition, for onsets within $\simeq0.2\,n_0$ of $n_m$. Relaxing maximal stiffness, we build EOSs with a transition at $\mu_{\rm tr}=1000$--$1300$~MeV, matched to perturbative QCD (pQCD) at $2.6$~GeV. pQCD limits the jump; EOSs compatible with PSR J0740+6620, J1614$-$2230, J0437$-$4715, J0614$-$3329, GW170817, and XTE J1814-338 appear only at $\mu_{\rm tr}=1200$ and $1250$~MeV; and inside the causal window, the largest jump agrees with the bound within the grid resolution. Finally, inserting a transition at $2.01\,\Msun$ into hadronic EOSs that satisfy five pulsar observations, the EOS with the lowest break density gives a narrow stable hybrid window ($\Delta M\simeq0.005\,\Msun$), compatible with XTE J1814-338 for jumps of $6$--$8\,n_0$ and with pQCD; three EOSs with higher break densities give none.

repl.title: Kratos-polrad: Novel GPU system for Monte-Carlo simulations with consistent polarization calculations
repl.summary: Polarized radiation serves as a vital diagnostic tool in astrophysics, providing unique insights into magnetic field geometries, scattering processes, and three-dimensional structures in diverse astrophysical scenarios. To address these applications, we present Kratos_polrad, a novel GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo Radiative Transfer code built upon the heterogeneous computing framework of Kratos, designed for self-consistent and efficient polarization calculations. It utilizes a comprehensive treatment of the Stokes parameters throughout photon propagation, featuring grain-lab frame transformations using quaternion algebra and a consistent analytical integration of polarized extinction and emission within each cell, which are useful in modeling radiative transfer processes with scatterings by aligned dust grains. The code implements two-step polarimetry imaging that decouples Monte Carlo sampling of scattering physics from imaging geometry, enabling efficient synthesis maximizing the utilization of photon packets. Extensive validation against analytical solutions and established codes demonstrates accurate treatment of diverse polarization phenomena, including self-scattering polarization, dichroic extinction in aligned dust grains, and complex polarization patterns in twisted magnetic field configurations. By leveraging massive GPU parallelism, optimized memory access patterns, and analytical approaches for optically thick cells, Kratos_polrad achieves performance improvements of ~10^2 times compared to CPU-based methods, enabling previously prohibitive studies in polarimetric astrophysics.

repl.title: MAMMOTH-LyC: Investigating the Role of Galaxy Mergers in a Strong Lyman Continuum Leaker at $z=2.39$
repl.summary: The MAMMOTH-LyC survey is a cycle 30 Hubble Space Telescope (HST) medium program obtaining 18-orbit-deep WFC3/UVIS F225W imaging in two massive galaxy protocluster fields at $z\sim2.2$. We introduce this survey by reporting the discovery of J1244-LyC1, a strong Lyman continuum (LyC) leaker at $z = 2.39$, exhibiting clear merger signatures. J1244-LyC1 has a highly significant ($6\sigma$) LyC detection, corresponding to an absolute escape fraction of $f_{\mathrm{esc}} \! =\!36\%\pm6\%$ ($1\sigma$). The LyC emission is spatially resolved into multiple peaks that coincide with the system's disturbed morphology, confirming genuine multi-site LyC leakage. With a stellar mass of $10^{10.2}{M_\odot}$, J1244-LyC1 is both the first confirmed high-redshift LyC-leaking merger and the most massive LyC emitter known to date. We interpret J1244-LyC1 as a merger-driven starburst system in which tidal interactions have disrupted the interstellar medium, creating multiple low-column-density pathways that facilitate LyC escape. This discovery provides the first direct evidence of spatially resolved LyC escape in a merging system, offering new insight into the potential role of major mergers in driving the cosmic reionization.

repl.title: Formation and Evolution of [Wolf-Rayet] Planetary Nebulae through a Late Thermal Pulse
repl.summary: We present the first radiation-hydrodynamical simulations of the formation of a born-again planetary nebula (PN) triggered by a late thermal pulse (LTP). The 2D radiation-hydrodynamic simulations, performed with the {\sc pluto} code, have been consistently coupled to stellar evolution calculations using the Modules for Experiments in Stellar Astrophysics ({\sc mesa}) code. Very particularly the stellar evolution model uses (i) updated opacity tables for H-deficient, C-rich mixtures during the LTP, and (ii) a mass-loss prescription tailored for H-deficient [Wolf-Rayet]([WR])-type winds during the post-LTP phase. Our stellar model reproduces the nearly complete depletion of H expected after an LTP event, while matching the observed abundances and spectral types of iconic [WR]-type central stars of PNe. The simulations show for the first time that the H-deficient LTP ejecta forms a transient double-shell structure which, after $\sim$1000 yr, becomes fully mixed with the H-rich PN. The ejecta mass ($\sim3.4\times10^{-4}$~M$_\odot$) is too small to leave a lasting imprint on the nebular abundances, predicting H-rich PNe around [WR] central stars. The injection of LTP material into the hot bubble drives turbulence, clump formation, and enhanced mixing, providing an explanation to the larger expansion velocities and larger turbulent nebular structures of PNe with [WR] central stars compared to those with H-rich central stars. These results provide robust support for the born-again scenario as the origin of H-deficient [WR] central stars within H-rich PNe.

repl.title: An empirical derivation of the average dust attenuation law at 2<z<7
repl.summary: Dust attenuation affects galaxy SEDs and introduces uncertainties in star formation rates, stellar masses, and metallicities. Direct spectroscopic constraints at early cosmic epochs were limited before JWST. We derive the average dust attenuation law of massive (log10(Mstar/Msun) > 9) star-forming galaxies at 2 < z < 7 using JWST spectroscopy. We combine JWST/NIRSpec spectroscopy from JADES with deep multi-wavelength photometry from the ASTRODEEP-JWST catalogues. For approximately 120 mass-selected galaxies with reliable Balmer decrement (Halpha/Hbeta) measurements, we stack SEDs in bins of Balmer optical depth and derive the selective attenuation curve following Calzetti et al. (1994). JWST/MIRI photometry extends the wavelength coverage into the near-infrared (NIR). The resulting curve spans 0.16-1.14 microns in the rest frame and is well described by a smooth function. We derive R_V approximately 3.98, with Delta R_V = 0.16 indicating its sensitivity to the adopted long-wavelength extrapolation. The average attenuation law agrees remarkably well with the local starburst relation in slope and normalisation, but appears systematically flatter in the ultraviolet than several intermediate-redshift determinations. We find no significant evidence for a 2175 Angstrom UV bump. Our results provide a direct empirical constraint on the average dust attenuation law of massive star-forming galaxies at 2 < z < 7. This analysis exploits the combined spectroscopic and photometric reach of JWST. Despite variations among individual galaxies, the ensemble-average behaviour agrees with the local starburst relation, suggesting that the main mechanisms governing dust attenuation were already operating at early cosmic times. The relatively shallow UV slope may reflect differences in dust-star geometry, radiative-transfer effects, or effective grain-size distributions among galaxy populations.

repl.title: Silicate cosmic dust grain collisions in the interstellar medium: A molecular dynamics study
repl.summary: (abridged) We aim to predict the most important parameters for grain-grain collision outcomes in models of interstellar grain population evolution: the threshold velocities for shattering and vaporization, and the resulting distributions of grain sizes. We use molecular dynamics simulations which evolve the dynamics of each atom in a dust grain to explore the outcomes of collisions between silicate grains of radii $a \in [5,50]~Å$ at velocities 0.1-20 km/s. We run simulations of grains with two materials: amorphous SiO$_2$ and an amorphous silicate of composition suggested by Draine \& Hensley (2021). With these simulations, we quantify the collision velocity dependence of shattered and vaporized mass fractions, and the resulting size distributions of shattering products. We find grain shattering thresholds are $\sim$6 km/s for both materials, a factor of $\sim$2 higher than the canonical value for silicates of 2.7 km/s from Tielens et al. (1994) and Jones et al. (1996). The size distributions of shattered products are generally not consistent with the power law distributions predicted by Jones et al. (1996), but the physical reasons for these discrepancies remain uncertain. The Tielens et al. (1994) expressions fail to predict the fraction of shattered or vaporized material observed in our numerical simulations, over-predicting the shattered fraction and under-predicting the vaporized fraction, except for the most massive grains we simulate, where the predicted vaporized fraction agrees reasonably well. The model of Hirashita \& Kobayashi (2013) similarly fails to match the simulations. We provide updated shattering velocity thresholds for nanoscale silicate grains, which suggest that the smallest astrophysical dust grains composed of silicate materials may be more robust to shattering in the interstellar medium than previously assumed.

repl.title: The Life and Death of Stars That Capture Primordial Black Holes
repl.summary: Primordial black holes (PBHs) in the asteroid mass window ($10^{17}-10^{23}\,{\rm g}$) remain viable dark matter candidates and can be captured by stars. We develop the first global framework for the evolution of stars that capture PBHs, combining analytic calculations, stellar evolution models, 3D general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamic simulations, and Monte Carlo population synthesis. We find that the fate of these systems bifurcates: PBHs that form an accretion disk before consuming the host drive explosive disruption, whereas PBHs captured too late or growing too slowly consume the star quietly. Capture is dominated by three-body interactions with planetary or stellar companions. For a solar-type host with a Jupiter analog, inspiral within a main-sequence lifetime requires $M_{\rm BH}^{\rm crit}\gtrsim 10^{22}\,{\rm g}$, while lighter PBHs generally require tighter companions. Once deposited at the center, the PBH grows through inefficient quasi-spherical Bondi accretion; if it reaches the angular-momentum threshold before consuming the host, the inflow circularizes into a disk. Our Monte Carlo calculations yield sizable quiet-consumption and explosive-disruption populations, with final PBH masses $M_{\rm BH}\sim0.01-1\,M_\odot$ and disk-forming PBH spins $a_\ast\approx0.8$. Disk formation is the point of no return: disk winds and relativistic jets of $\sim10^{45}-10^{50}\,{\rm erg\,s^{-1}}$ disrupt the star within minutes. The resulting transients may include a $\sim$day-long UV/blue signal, radio afterglow, and, if the jet escapes, an X-ray-flash/low-luminosity gamma-ray-burst (XRF/llGRB) signal. For an $O(1)$ PBH dark matter fraction and optimistic capture assumptions, the event rate can reach that of llGRBs. The low-mass, high-spin remnants offer a complementary PBH probe and possible source for subsolar BH mergers.

repl.title: The Effect of Adiabatic Index on Radius Evolution and the Mass Loss
repl.summary: Models that track the size evolution of exoplanets often assume a prescribed initial thermal state or a single adiabatic index to describe the planetary interior structure, the latter of which is taken to be $\gamma \sim1.4$ which is likely appropriate for evolved planets ($\gtrsim$1 Gyr). Extrapolating this high $\gamma$ to earlier ages (down to $\sim$million years old) is problematic since, according to thermodynamics, the adiabatic index of young planets is $\sim$1.2, which is low enough to drastically change how interior mass is distributed. We quantify the effect of varying the adiabatic index from 1.2 to 1.4 on the expected radius of the exoplanet over time. We find that envelopes of larger adiabatic indices start puffier with all else equal and undergo faster radius contraction with accelerated mass loss. Assumption of high $\gamma$ can therefore overestimate the effect of mass loss in shaping the exoplanetary population, especially when young planets are considered. We highlight the need for a more careful consideration of the initial thermal condition of planets in evolutionary models to properly interpret the radii measurements of exoplanets.

repl.title: A New Scaling of Neutron Star Tidal Deformability for Directly Probing the Central Equation of State Parameter
repl.summary: The dimensionless tidal deformability, $\Lambda$, of neutron stars (NSs), inferred from gravitational-wave (GW) observations, has thus far been used primarily to constrain the pressure of dense matter near twice nuclear saturation density, leaving the core equation of state (EOS) largely inaccessible to inspiral-phase GW observations. We show that a fundamental central EOS parameter can be probed directly through $\Lambda$ using a perturbative analysis of the dimensionless stellar-structure and tidal-response equations formulated in terms of scaled intrinsic variables, without invoking any specific EOS model. We uncover a remarkable EOS-insensitive scaling relation between $\Lambda$ and the central EOS parameter $\rm{X}\equiv P_{\rm c}/\varepsilon_{\rm c}$, where $P_{\rm c}$ and $\varepsilon_{\rm c}$ denote the central pressure and energy density, respectively. The relation is validated against a broad ensemble of physically viable EOSs. Applying it to tidal deformabilities inferred from events such as GW170817 enables a direct determination of $\rm{X}$. By adopting the previously established effective upper bound $\rm{X}\lesssim0.381$, we infer a tight lower bound, $\Lambda_{\rm{TOV}}\gtrsim9.1^{+0.5}_{-0.5}$, for maximum-mass NSs along stable mass-radius sequences, quantitatively demonstrating that even the most compact stable NSs remain distinctly separated from black holes, for which $\Lambda_{\rm{BH}}=0$. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized connection between inspiral-phase tidal deformability and the central EOS parameter $\rm{X}$, establishing a direct link between GW observables and the microphysics of ultradense matter in the strong-gravity regime. The resulting scaling establishes inspiral-phase tidal deformability as a direct and largely model-insensitive probe of the central EOS parameter $\rm{X}$, and hence of key properties of NS cores.

repl.title: Search for Diffuse Supernova Neutrino Background in the Full KamLAND Dataset with Neural-Network-Based Event Classification
repl.summary: We report a search for the diffuse supernova neutrino background (DSNB) with the KamLAND detector, targeting electron antineutrinos via inverse beta decay in the neutrino energy range of 8.3 to 30.8 MeV. Using liquid-scintillator exposures of 9.02 kton-year for 8.3 to 9.3 MeV and 9.42 kton-year for 9.3 to 30.8 MeV, we observe seven candidate events after applying a new deep-neural-network-based event classification technique. This result is consistent with the background-only expectation of 16.2 plus or minus 9.4 events, including systematic uncertainties associated with the neural-network selection. A spectral analysis of the energy and radial distributions finds no significant excess attributable to the DSNB. We therefore set 90 percent confidence-level upper limits on the DSNB flux of 38 to 43 per square centimeter per second, depending on the assumed DSNB model. We also derive model-independent 90 percent confidence-level upper limits on the electron-antineutrino flux, obtaining some of the most stringent constraints below 13.3 MeV. Beyond the DSNB search itself, this work demonstrates neural-network-based event classification as a promising approach for suppressing neutron-associated backgrounds in liquid-scintillator neutrino detectors.

repl.title: Unveiling the Milky Way with a Gaia DR3 census of OB-type stars within 2 kpc. I. Tracing local Galactic structure, massive star-forming regions and core-collapse supernova progenitors
repl.summary: O- and B-type stars are young and hot, thereby serving as vital tracers of the star formation and spiral arm structure of the Milky Way. At the dusk of the \textit{Gaia} DR3 era, a high-confidence and accurate catalogue appears timely. We have characterized 105,971 OB-type stars (T$_{\rm eff} >$ 10,000 K) within 2 kpc from the Sun, using an astro-photometric Bayesian inference tool. Our map unveils a complex view of the young stellar populations across the thin disk, with prominent large-scale features such as the Cepheus Spur, the Giant Oval Cavity, and a segment the Sagittarius-Carina arm all visible. Their inhomogeneous spatial distribution implies that massive star formation has taken place clustered across a few highly concentrated regions. We find a correlation between the overdensities of OB-type stars and young open clusters, and attribute departure from it to extinction effects. We identify 4200 stars as model-dependent core-collapse supernova (ccSN) or direct-collapse black hole (BH) progenitor candidates, including 6 ccSN progenitor candidates within 125 pc -- the maximum radius within which a ccSN explosion could be harmful to Earth's biosphere -- but our analysis suggests none of them exploding within the next 5 Myrs. Finally, we anticipate more evolved OB-type stars to collapse to form BHs within the next 1 Myr than ccSN progenitors will explode, despite the former's much scarcer number. A possible interpretation is a recent star formation burst in the local Milky Way, consistent with overdensities of ccSN progenitor candidates in Cyg OB2 and the Sagittarius-Carina arm.

repl.title: Infrasound Newtonian Noise Estimation at the Einstein Telescope Candidate Site Sos Enattos
repl.summary: We investigate the seasonal variability of atmospheric infrasound and its contribution to Newtonian noise (NN) at the Sos Enattos site, a leading candidate location for the Einstein Telescope (ET). Infrasound data recorded at three stations, SOE0 (surface), SOE1 ($-84$ m) and SOE3 ($-160$ m), are analysed over multiple seasons to characterise both the temporal variability and the depth dependence of the acoustic field. At the surface, the median amplitude spectral density (ASD) at 1 Hz shows no consistent seasonal modulation, and its variability is driven primarily by wind; the apparent dependence on sea state largely reflects its correlation with wind speed. Underground, where local wind noise is suppressed, a winter maximum of 4--7 dB above the quietest season is observed in both years of data. Using the measured sound-pressure spectra, we estimate the corresponding NN contribution for an underground cavern with the dimensions foreseen for ET, assuming an isotropic field of acoustic plane waves. The surface pressure field, acting through the atmosphere above a test mass at 200 m depth, exceeds the ET-D design sensitivity in median conditions between 1.6 and 7.1 Hz, by up to a factor of 4.7. Inside the cavern, the median NN remains a factor of 1.4 below ET-D with the pressure measured at SOE1, but exceeds it between 2.5 and 8.7 Hz, by up to a factor of 3.5, with the pressure measured at SOE3. The attenuation is not monotonic with depth: the deeper station SOE3 shows higher levels than SOE1 above a few hertz, pointing to local, anthropogenic sources in the underground infrastructure. These results show that underground placement is essential but not sufficient on its own, and that the acoustic emission of the underground infrastructure and future laboratory equipment will require careful evaluation and mitigation to keep atmospheric NN below the ET design sensitivity.

repl.title: Observational Evidence for Anisotropic Metal Excess around Galaxies
repl.summary: The exchange of matter and energy between galaxies and their surroundings drives the cosmic baryon cycle, yet mapping metal transport remains an observational challenge. While simulations predict that galactic winds escape anisotropically along minor axes, evidence for chemical enrichment in neighboring galaxies is limited. We analyze 1,433 galaxy pairs from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument survey and detect a gas-phase metallicity excess of 14.6% $\pm$ 3.7% to 24.2% $\pm$ 2.6% in neighbors aligned with the minor axis of massive primary at projected separations of 15--60 kpc, qualitatively consistent with IllustrisTNG simulation. Permutation tests indicate that this excess varies from a marginal detection ($>$92% confidence) at closer separations (15--30 kpc) to a significant signal ($>$98% confidence) at intermediate separations (30--60 kpc). Here, we show that these results provide empirical constraints on galactic feedback models and are consistent with a scenario where anisotropic outflows can enrich nearby galaxies, a mechanism that complements other environmental processes.

repl.title: VAPOLA - A multiyear, multiband polarization survey of AGNs and Sgr A* at millimeter wavelengths with ALMA II. Spectropolarimetric properties and their evolution from 2017 to 2023
repl.summary: We present a systematic analysis of the spectropolarimetric properties of a sample of 39 active galactic nuclei and Sagittarius A* observed with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array during five VLBI campaigns between 2017 and 2023. We characterize the compact cores in total intensity and polarization, focusing on the behavior or the linear polarization fraction (LP), electric vector position angle (EVPA), and Faraday rotation measure (RM) over time and spectral domains. We investigate both individual objects--such as M87, Sgr A*, 3C273, and 3C279--and ensemble properties of different source classes, including flat-spectrum radio quasars, BLLac objects, and other active galaxies. While total intensity and spectral index are generally stable on weekly timescales, polarization properties often exhibit strong variability, with significant day-to-day changes in LP, EVPA, and RM. Several sources display large EVPA rotations accompanied by variations in LP and RM, in some cases coinciding with flaring activity. We observe that the magnitude of RM increases with observing frequency for all sources for which we have reliable multi-band measurements, consistent with Faraday rotation arising in a magnetized sheath surrounding the relativistic jet, although an origin in the accretion flow--particularly in the case of Sgr A*--cannot be ruled out.
