repl.title: Periodic activity on the (sub)mm surface of the AGB star Mira A
repl.summary: Evolved stars on the asymptotic giant branch (AGB) lose mass through stellar winds launched from their dynamic extended atmospheres. Recent high-angular-resolution observations of the archetypal AGB star Mira A (o Ceti) have revealed compact hotspots on its (sub)millimetre surface, whose origin remains unclear. We aim to characterise the (sub)millimetre photosphere of Mira A and investigate the properties and temporal behaviour of the compact hotspots detected on its surface. We analysed 19 epochs of high-angular-resolution observations obtained with ALMA in Bands 4, 6, 7, and 9. The complex visibilities were fitted with parametric models to derive the flux density, size, morphology, and brightness temperature of the stellar disc and an additional, more compact component across multiple pulsation phases and observing frequencies. Our results show that, near maximum light, the flux density of the stellar disc increases with frequency while its apparent size decreases, in agreement with the expected stratified radio photosphere. In Band 6, both the flux density and the size of the stellar disc appear to vary with pulsation phase, with the largest measured values occurring close to optical maximum light and the lowest observed around minimum light. Compact hotspots are detected in Bands 6 and 7 near maximum light, with their brightness temperatures exceeding those of the stellar disc by several thousand kelvin and reaching a temperature excess of ~8200 K in Band 6. They are highly energetic and are detected over timescales of weeks, while the available observations also suggest potential longer-term changes in both their position and intensity. Hotspot activity appears to occur repeatedly across multiple pulsation cycles and may be linked to strong shocks, magnetic activity, and/or episodic mass ejections, and could therefore play an important role in the mass-loss process in AGB stars.

repl.title: Wide Field Localization Using Fixed Modulation Collimators
repl.summary: Rapid, precise localization of gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) requires continuous wide-field imaging at hard X-ray and soft gamma-ray energies. We develop a fixed (non-rotating) modulation-collimator architecture to address this challenge. A bigrid collimator, a pair of aligned, periodic slit grids in front of a simple, non-imaging photon-counting detector, transmits an off-axis source through a triangular fringe pattern whose local angular position, the source phase, is recovered from simultaneous count rates in several grid pairs at fixed relative phase offsets, rather than by mechanically rotating a single grid pair as in the classical rotating modulation collimator. Four-phase demodulation of these count rates robustly cancels detector background and grid leakage without requiring rotation. Because the fringe pattern repeats across the sky, a phase measurement corresponds to many candidate source positions; we resolve this ambiguity over an arbitrarily wide field of view using a cascade of progressively coarser-pitched grid stages, generalizing the two-grid vernier-scale technique originally used to localize Sco X-1. This vernier cascade technique reduces the required photon counts and grid-calibration accuracy required to achieve fine angular resolution over a broad field of view. Generalized to two dimensions with orthogonal cascades, the resulting architecture achieves wide-field localization with no moving parts, no time modulation, and only simple photon-counting detectors, a promising candidate for simple, inexpensive, continuous-monitoring instruments supporting time-domain and multi-messenger astrophysics.

repl.title: Thermal Evolution of Lava Planets Across System Ages: Predictions for Hell of a Survey
repl.summary: Ultra-short-period (USP) rocky exoplanets can have dayside temperatures high enough to maintain permanent magma oceans, sitting at the intersection of interior geophysics and atmospheric chemistry. Coupled feedbacks between the molten surface and outgassed atmosphere can sustain or enhance a volatile envelope, while stellar interactions can erode it. Understanding which outcome prevails, and its observable imprint, requires a multi-target approach across planets at different stages of thermal evolution. We present predictions for the five targets of JWST Cycle 4 program 8864: TOI-1807 b, TOI-2260 b, TOI-431 b, TOI-6255 b, and TOI-2431 b. Using the PROTEUS coupled interior-atmosphere framework, we construct a simulation grid and classify outcomes into six categories, defined by the final interior melt state and by whether the planet retains a detectable atmosphere thick enough to redistribute heat to the nightside. For targets retaining a non-negligible volatile envelope, our models predict higher partial pressures for most species when the surface is molten, except for S$_{2}$, whose enhancement in the solid regime suggests it may serve as a tracer of interior melt state. Despite some targets showing outcomes across multiple scenarios, most tend toward a bare-rock end-member, with global melt fraction $\leq$ 20\% and atmospheric retention sensitive to escape efficiency. Our analysis reveals a minimum escape efficiency threshold below which volatile envelopes survive under energy-limited escape, constraining the conditions required for atmosphere survival on irradiated rocky planets. These predictions will guide interpretation of MIRI-LRS phase curve observations and identify which targets and features best discriminate between competing geophysical states.

repl.title: Solar spicule population properties inferred from IRIS Mg II k off-limb spectra using likelihood-free Bayesian inference
repl.summary: Solar spicules are ubiquitous and strongly overlap in off-limb observations, which complicates the interpretation of individual events. We aim to infer population-level properties of spicules from IRIS Mg II k off-limb spectra using a forward model that explicitly accounts for line-of-sight superposition and instrumental effects. We constructed a stochastic 3D spicule-population model and synthesized Mg II k spectra with radiative transfer, including instrumental degradation and photon noise. We then constrained the hyperparameters that describe the underlying spicule population with likelihood-free Bayesian inference. This approach combines approximate Bayesian computation and an adaptive population Monte Carlo sampler, comparing observed and simulated datasets through principal-component summary statistics at five heights above the limb. The inferred posterior constrains effective population-level properties of the spicules that dominate the observed Mg II k variability and height dependence. These constraints provide a route to connect off-limb spectroscopy with forthcoming spectropolarimetric diagnostics of the chromosphere--corona interface.

repl.title: Galaxy Protoclusters as Drivers of Cosmic Reionization: II. Te-Based Metallicities of Lyman-α Emitters
repl.summary: Context. Protoclusters at reionization are thought to host a significant fraction of the cosmic star formation rate density, making them crucial for the timing and topology of reionization. The gas-phase metallicity, a key tracer of galaxy evolutionary stage, can now be measured directly in the early Universe with JWST. Aims. We measure the gas-phase metallicity of Lyman-$\alpha$ emitters (LAEs) in the LAGER-z7OD1 protocluster at $z\approx6.93$ via the direct ($T_e$-based) method using the [O III]$\lambda$4363 auroral line, and combine it with stellar masses to constrain the mass-metallicity relation (MZR) in dense environments. Methods. We use JWST/NIRSpec MSA G395H spectroscopy, derive metallicities with self-consistent analytic prescriptions, and propagate the dust-extinction uncertainty into an asymmetric error budget via Monte Carlo simulations based on the observed Balmer decrements. Stellar masses come from BEAGLE SED fitting of JWST/NIRCam and UltraVISTA photometry. Results. We obtain five secure [O III]$\lambda$4363 detections and one upper limit, with 12+log(O/H) $\approx$ 7.2-8.0. The weighted spectral stack yields 12+log(O/H) = $7.76^{+0.06}_{-0.05}$, ~0.26 dex higher than stacks of LAEs at similar redshifts from JWST surveys. However, the MZR fit gives a slope $\gamma$ = 0.232 +/- 0.214 and normalization $Z_0$ = 7.888 +/- 0.199, placing our sources below the established MZR of normal galaxies and recent protocluster baselines at $z\sim5-7$. Conclusions. The higher metallicity relative to general LAEs suggests accelerated assembly driven by the overdensity, while the offset below the MZR points to a complex interplay between mass build-up and gas accretion. Since we target actively star-forming LAEs, we are likely capturing a phase of pristine gas inflow from the intergalactic medium that fuels star formation but dilutes the interstellar media of these protocluster members.

repl.title: Collisional excitation of SiC$_6$ by helium: cross sections, rate coefficients, and astrophysical implications
repl.summary: Rotational transitions of SiC$_6$ with $j=26$--$40$ have been detected in IRC+10216, but collisional rate coefficients for SiC$_6$ with He or H$_2$ were previously unavailable. We present rate coefficients for SiC$_6$ rotational excitation by He, calculated using a two-dimensional potential energy surface (PES) at the RCCSD(T)-F12 level under the rigid-rotor approximation. Close-coupling (CC) calculations were performed for low rotational levels, while the coupled-states (CS) method was used for higher levels. Convergence tests were conducted, and CC and CS scattering cross sections were compared. The CS rate coefficients cover rotational levels up to $j=40$ and temperatures of 3--60\,K. Although CC and CS rate coefficients differ by up to a factor of $\sim 2$ for some transitions, particularly those affected by weak coupling and resonances, they yield nearly identical excitation and brightness temperatures for the high-$j$ transitions examined, including $19\rightarrow18$. These results support the reliability of the CS method for non-LTE modelling of the high-$j$ transitions considered, for which CC calculations are computationally impractical. We use reduced-mass scaling of the SiC$_6$--He rate coefficients to estimate those for SiC$_6$--H$_2$ and model the observed transitions. A $\chi^2$ analysis of the observed line fluxes, excluding heavily blended features, yields a best-fitting of $n(\mathrm{H_2})=4.33\times10^5$\,cm$^{-3}$ and $N(\mathrm{SiC_6})=8.11\times10^{11}$\,cm$^{-2}$. The latter agrees excellently with the previous observational estimate of $(7.9\pm1.5)\times10^{11}$\,cm$^{-2}$, supporting the consistency of our non-LTE modelling with observational constraints.

repl.title: A faint dust ring beyond the compact disk of Sz 76
repl.summary: We report new ALMA Band 7 high-resolution ($\sim$0.05$^{''}$) continuum and $^{12}\text{CO}\ (J=3\text{--}2)$ observations of the disk around the young low-mass star Sz 76. Visibility-plane modeling reveals a previously undetected, faint outer dust ring centered at $\sim$45 au surrounding the compact central disk. Including this low-surface-brightness feature increases the characteristic dust radius from $R_{\text{dust,68}} \approx 7$ au to $41$ au. Combined with an outer gas extent of $R_{\text{CO,68}} \approx 77$ au, the resulting gas-to-dust size ratio decreases from an extreme value of $\sim$11 to $\sim$2, placing Sz 76 in line with typical protoplanetary disks and contradicting a scenario of unimpeded inward radial drift. These results demonstrate that spatial filtering or limited surface-brightness sensitivity can severely underestimate disk sizes, highlighting the necessity of multi-scale observations to properly identify dust traps and accurately constrain disk evolution.

repl.title: Structure and evolution of cosmic voids within DESI DR1
repl.summary: Ongoing stage IV galaxy surveys such as DESI or Euclid offer an unprecedented amount of information to study the large-scale structure of the Universe by mapping tens of millions of galaxies. Within the context of cosmic voids, already released and future catalogues will help better understand the void structure and evolution as well as the cosmological model constraints derived from their statistics. With the recent DESI Data Release 1, our aim is to obtain a new void catalogue that allows us to study the properties of cosmic voids at different redshifts, hence providing insight not only on their structure but also on their evolution. We select the DESI BGS and LRG samples for this study. Before the void-finding process, the data goes through a preprocessing pipeline tackling redshift space distortions and reconstructing the mildly non-linear velocity field. After that, the new AVISM void finder is applied to the preprocessed data, obtaining two void catalogues in different redshift bins (0.1 < z < 0.3 and 0.4 < z < 0.8), both within a 1400^3 cMpc^3 cube. We successfully recover N_BGS = 1114 and N_LRG = 216 clean voids with sizes up to ~ 65 cMpc. The void size function, 3D shape variables, density profiles, and linear bias are obtained and analysed. Both the size function and the density profiles obtained are in agreement with previous theoretical studies. The expected mass depletion in void evolution is shown by the evolution of density profiles. We obtain a roughly constant linear bias inside r < Re with mean values of 1.31 +/- 0.02 and 2.14 +/- 0.04 for BGS and LRG, respectively. Both void catalogues are publicly released.

repl.title: Optical constraints on intranight variability in TeV HBLs from a two-year Asiago Schmidt monitoring campaign
repl.summary: We present a two-year homogeneous optical monitoring campaign of three TeV-emitting high-synchrotron-peaked BL Lac objects, 1ES 1959+650, H 1426+428, and PG 1553+113, carried out with the Asiago Schmidt 67/92 cm telescope. TeV blazars are key targets in high-energy astrophysics, relevant for relativistic jet physics, particle acceleration, multiwavelength variability studies, and, in selected cases, multimessenger programmes. In this context, dense optical monitoring provides a low-energy synchrotron tracer of jet activity over temporal baselines that are difficult to cover continuously with high-energy facilities. The dataset consists of more than 17,000 R- and I-band photometric measurements obtained over 957 source-filter observing sessions between 2024 February 1 and 2026 January 31, for a total monitoring time of about 420 h. We applied a uniform differential-photometry and classical F-test framework based on two independent comparison-star pairs. Robust IDV is detected only in H 1426+428, with 15 out of 43 analysed sessions classified as variable in the R band and 5 out of 40 in the I band. No significant IDV is detected in 1ES 1959+650 or PG 1553+113 within the adopted statistical framework. For H 1426+428, the corresponding duration-weighted duty cycles, computed using only variable sessions with a measured local characteristic timescale, are 28.0% in the R band and 7.0% in the I band. The inferred local extrapolated doubling/halving timescales are of the order of 5-15 min in the observer frame. These results indicate that rapid optical synchrotron variability in TeV HBLs is intermittent and state-dependent. They also show that robotic small- and medium-aperture optical facilities can provide valuable long-term support for high-energy monitoring programmes by supplying dense, uniform, and repeatable optical coverage.

repl.title: Consistently Reproducing Early Galaxy Observations and 21-cm Signal during the Epoch of Reionization
repl.summary: In the standard cosmological model, galaxies forming within dark matter haloes are the primary drivers of the Epoch of Reionization (EoR). The complex physics of galaxy formation introduces scatter in the relation between halo mass and star-formation activity, with implications for the production and escape of ionising photons. In this work, we implement a stochastic source model in our cosmological radiative transfer simulations. We calibrate our model against the high-redshift ultraviolet luminosity function observed by JWST and observational constraints on Lyman-continuum leakage to constrain the ionising escape fraction. We find that stochastic star formation redistributes ionising emissivity toward lower-mass haloes, producing a more fragmented ionisation topology and delaying the growth of the largest ionised regions relative to the deterministic, observationally calibrated model. However, when the two models match total ionising photon production, their global neutral fractions and 21-cm power spectrum remain nearly indistinguishable, despite small differences in the morphology of individual ionised regions. Additionally, we establish a unified framework that lets us apply source models derived from computationally expensive hydrodynamical simulations (SPICE, FIRE-2 and Thesan) and investigate their impact on large-volume reionisation simulations, extending their prescriptions to scales of >100 Mpc. We find that these prescriptions produce distinct ionisation topologies and 21-cm statistical signatures, even when their global reionisation histories are similar. Our results highlight the importance of combining physically motivated galaxy formation prescriptions from hydrodynamical simulations with large-volume radiative transfer simulations to interpret forthcoming 21-cm observations and constrain the sources of cosmic reionisation.

repl.title: Beyond the Disc--Spheroid Dichotomy at $0.6 < z < 8.0$: Evidence for a Morphological Indeterminacy Regime from JWST
repl.summary: Galaxy morphology is a fundamental tracer of galaxy assembly, but its characterization becomes increasingly uncertain in the early Universe. We investigate morphological classifications across different methodologies over the redshift range $0.6 < z < 8.0$, using JWST observations of 15,567 galaxies with 6,099 synthetic galaxies from IllustrisTNG. To quantify morphology without relying on visual labels or prescribed light profiles, we use an unsupervised-supervised hybrid machine-learning approach based on the non-parametric MEGG system, which combines the second moment of the light distribution, Entropy, Gini, and Gradient Pattern Analysis. We find that parametric and non-parametric classifications remain broadly consistent at $z < 2.5$, but diverge systematically at higher redshift. We identify this epoch as the Morphological Indeterminacy Regime (MIR), in which classical disc and spheroidal categories no longer provide a unique description of the galaxy population. The fraction of mixed-interpretation galaxies increases with redshift, reaching $F_{\rm MIR} \sim 0.55$ at $z > 2.5$. Cross-domain and projection-invariance tests show that the classifications are stable and insensitive to data set and viewing angle. In the interval $2.5 < z < 8.0$, MIR galaxies occupy an intermediate stellar-mass regime (median; $\log(M_\star/M_\odot) \sim 9.7$), between low-mass discs (median; $\log(M_\star/M_\odot) \sim 9.5$) and massive spheroids (median; $\log(M_\star/M_\odot) \sim 10.1$), while irregular systems have stellar-mass distributions similar to those of MIR galaxies. We interpret these results as evidence that morphological indeterminacy is a characteristic feature of galaxy assembly in the early Universe, reflecting a population of dynamically young systems that have not yet settled into the classical Hubble sequence.

repl.title: The DARWIN Project: Cosmological Simulations of Galaxy Formation down to Dwarf Scales in Diverse Environments
repl.summary: We present the DARWIN project, a suite of cosmological simulations with RAMSES to study dwarf-galaxy formation and evolution across diverse environments. DARWIN-1 is a full-box simulation in a cubic volume of $(65.5\,{\rm cMpc})^3$ with a minimum cell size of 500pc, while DARWIN-2 comprises zoom-in simulations of 24 field regions and a Milky Way analog connected to a filament, reaching 62.5pc resolution. The simulations employ baryonic physics tailored to their aims. For DARWIN-2, we include radiative transfer in three photon energy bands to trace hydrogen and helium ionization. DARWIN-1 reproduces the cosmic star formation rate density and galaxy stellar mass functions reasonably well at $z>1$. Both simulations broadly reproduce observed stellar mass-halo mass relations, chemical abundances, star-formation surface densities, and black hole-galaxy scaling relations. At lower redshift, DARWIN-1 shows an excess in the number density of massive galaxies, although the inferred stellar content of massive halos depends on the definition of galaxy stellar mass. Other systematic differences arise from spatial resolution, feedback efficiency, and environmental selection. To facilitate comparison with observations, we generate mock images using the radiative transfer codes SKIRT and Powderday. We also explore a machine-learning approach to mitigate resolution-driven biases in the dwarf galaxy properties of DARWIN-1 using the higher-resolution DARWIN-2 simulations. The DARWIN simulation suite therefore provides a comprehensive numerical framework for studying the formation, evolution, and internal physics of dwarf galaxies in a cosmological context.

repl.title: The Central Molecular Zone of our Galaxy, a chemical complexity factory: first interstellar detections of molecules towards G+0.693
repl.summary: The Central Molecular Zone (CMZ) of our Galaxy is a prime laboratory for interstellar chemistry because of its extreme conditions, such as shocks and high cosmic-ray ionisation rates. It is an efficient factory of molecules, with many species first discovered in CMZ sources. This document reviews key results from the study of the CMZ G+0.693-0.027 molecular cloud. Using ultra-sensitive broadband spectral surveys together with laboratory spectroscopy, more than 140 molecules have been identified, including 28 detected for the first time in the interstellar medium (ISM). These discoveries include prebiotic precursors of biomolecules, increasingly complex members of known molecular families, molecules containing periodic third-row elements (S, P, Na, Mg), high-energy stereo- and structural isomers, and new cations. Overall, these findings extend the known limits of interstellar chemical complexity and highlight the CMZ's potential to provide the molecular ingredients for prebiotic chemistry.

repl.title: New Bounds on Heavy QCD Axions from Big Bang Nucleosynthesis
repl.summary: We study Big Bang Nucleosynthesis (BBN) constraints on heavy QCD axions. BBN offers a powerful probe of new physics that modifies the neutron-to-proton ratio during the process, thanks to the precisely measured primordial Helium-4 abundance. A heavy QCD axion provides an attractive target for this probe, because not only is it a well-motivated hypothetical particle by the strong CP problem, but also it dominantly decays to hadrons if kinematically allowed. A range of its lifetime is thus excluded where the hadronic decays would significantly alter the neutron-to-proton ratio. We compute axion-induced modification of the neutron-to-proton ratio, and obtain robust upper bounds on the axion lifetimes, as low as 0.017 s for the axion mass higher than 300 MeV. Remarkably, this is stronger than projected future CMB bounds via $N_{\rm eff}$. Our bounds are largely insensitive to uncertainties in hadronic cross sections and the axion's branching fractions into various hadrons, as well as to the precise value of the initial axion abundance. We also incorporate, for the first time, several key improvements, such as scattering processes by energetic $K_L$ and secondary hadrons, that can also be important for studying general hadronic injections during BBN, not limited to those from axion decays.

repl.title: Inflationary Particle Production and the Swampland
repl.summary: We investigate the impact of particle production during inflation in scenarios where an infinite tower of states features a mass scale that decreases exponentially along the inflationary trajectory. Such couplings naturally arise in string effective field theories and are in fact motivated by the Swampland Distance Conjecture (SDC). We show that the corrections to inflationary observables sourced by the tower scale as $(H/\Lambda_{\text{sp}})^{2+p}$, with $H$ being the Hubble scale, $\Lambda_{\text{sp}}$ being the species scale, that is the quantum gravity cut-off, and $p\geq 1$ characterizes the density of states in the tower. As a result, in gravitationally weakly coupled cosmological effective theories, the tower-induced contributions are suppressed relative to the standard single-field predictions, leaving the inflationary phenomenology essentially unchanged. We demonstrate this explicitly across a set of well-motivated inflationary potentials, and we compare the resulting predictions with the most recent observational constraints, including those from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope.

repl.title: Probing freeze-in dark matter using Bose-Einstein condensate in neutron star
repl.summary: Neutron star (NS) is one of the most promising astrophysical targets to probe non-gravitational interaction of dark matter (DM) with visible matter. Their compactness makes them an ideal object which can capture particle DM efficiently over its lifetime using the DM-nucleon scattering cross-section. If DM particles are bosonic, then the captured DM population may form a Bose-Einstein condensate at the center of the NS, increasing the DM density significantly. In this work, we study the phenomenology of such scenario with enhanced DM annihilation rate due to the increased density in a condensate. The enhanced DM annihilation makes the NS surface `hotter' than in the standard cooling scenario. We show that the annihilation rate is enhanced by a factor of $\mathcal{O}(10^{15}-10^{20})$ if DM forms a condensate without large self-interaction, and DM with freeze-in value annihilation cross-section can heat up the NS to higher temperatures, bringing it within the reach of James Webb Space Telescope. It also allows us to probe DM-nucleon scattering cross section within the neutrino fog regime which will complement the terrestrial direct detection searches. Moreover, the enhanced annihilation from the condensate changes the lower limits on s-wave DM annihilation cross-section for capture-annihilation equilibrium and the formation of a black hole inside the NS. Finally, we show an example of a scalar DM model where such small annihilation and DM-nucleon scattering cross sections can generically arise.

repl.title: Energy extraction from NED-deformed rotating black holes via the Comisso-Asenjo reconnection process
repl.summary: We study rotating black holes in general relativity coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics (NED), focusing on an axisymmetric solution with deformation parameter $g$. On the spherical seed, weak-field lensing via the Gauss-Bonnet method and the shadow radius yield a spin-insensitive bound by enforcing a conservative $\sim 10\%$ tolerance on the Sgr A* ring size, namely $g/M \lesssim 1.26$. In the eikonal regime we derive analytic quasinormal-mode shifts, even in $g$, and obtain an independent ceiling consistent with the shadow constraint. For the rotating geometry, we provide closed-form ZAMO scalars, chart horizons and the ergoregion, and analyze equatorial geodesics (photon orbits and ISCO). We then formulate the Comisso-Asenjo reconnection channel in the ZAMO frame, identify the negative-energy window, and integrate the extracted power over the allowed radii; from the tolerated fractional departure from the Kerr power we define a spin-dependent extraction bound $g_\delta(a\mid\sigma_0,\xi)$. Taken together, the QNM/shadow ceiling and the extraction bound appreciably narrow the admissible region for $g/M$ in the $(a/M,g/M)$ plane, so even within our deliberately simplified, single-layer equatorial setup, the two complementary probes already provide informative constraints on NED deformations, testable with present data and upcoming horizon-scale and ringdown campaigns.

repl.title: Detecting Tidal Resonances in Binary Neutron Stars
repl.summary: As a binary neutron star inspirals due to the emission of gravitational waves, the rising tidal frequency resonantly excites vibrational modes. These oscillations are seismological probes of the rich stellar interior, yet it remains to be established whether gravitational-wave interferometers can measure them. Here, we present the first fully Bayesian study of the capability of the Einstein Telescope to detect tidal resonances. We simulate one year of observations and analyse the 200 loudest signals. We find that the Einstein Telescope can identify resonant modes and is sensitive to gravitational-wave phase shifts as small as $\Delta \Phi \approx 0.03$ for favourable events. We further show that neglecting resonances can bias the inferred tidal deformabilities. These results establish tidal resonances as a measurable route for asteroseismology with future detectors.

repl.title: A dark-matter-sensitive orientation clock near rotating black holes
repl.summary: A coherent triaxial structure has an intrinsic orientation clock because rotation about its intermediate principal axis is unstable. I ask how this clock changes when the structure moves on a circular equatorial orbit near a rotating black hole in an effective dark matter (DM) environment. The calculation uses a comoving orthonormal tetrad, the electric part of the Riemann tensor, Euler--quaternion dynamics, and the conversion from proper time to stationary coordinate time. The clock shift separates exactly into a local proper-time response and a geometric time-conversion response. I compute a direct grid of 600 DM models for Einasto, regularized cored Navarro--Frenk--White, and Hernquist profiles. Across the scanned domain, the total fractional frequency shift lies between about $-3\times10^{-7}$ and $-3\times10^{-4}$. For the fiducial body model, most of the shift comes from the time conversion. Synthetic timing tests show that a shift near $10^{-4}$ is recoverable only when the clock is highly coherent and its Kerr baseline is known independently. This gives a theoretical timing diagnostic and a synthetic observational forecast. I do not fit real data.

repl.title: Resonant lunar tides of Earth's core and basal magma ocean
repl.summary: Earth's magnetic field is generated by fluid motion in the liquid-metal core and has been active for billions of years. However, prior to the onset of inner-core growth, the sources of mechanical power that drove the geodynamo remain uncertain. During this period, the core may have been overlain by a basal magma ocean (BMO), creating two immiscible fluid layers separated by a density interface, beneath the solid mantle. We develop a theory for lunar tides in this core--BMO system, in which the tidal potential acts on the density contrast between the two layers. The resulting dynamics differ fundamentally from previous models driven by imposed deformation of the core's bounding envelope. In the inviscid limit, the response transitions from an equilibrium tide to an interfacial gravity wave as forcing frequency increases. The two regimes are separated by a resonance that occurs when the forcing frequency matches the natural frequency of the degree-2, order-2 interfacial mode. The inviscid core flow is formally identical to the canonical elliptical vortex, linking the problem to the theory of elliptical instability. Finite viscosity regularises the resonance, introduces phase lag and generates oscillatory boundary layers. Combined with parameterised models of lunar recession and BMO crystallisation, the theory predicts enhanced core-boundary ellipticity, core-flow speed, magnetic Reynolds number and instability metrics, particularly near resonance. These results identify a previously unexplored mechanism for tidally driven flow in differentiated planetary bodies and show that a BMO can enhance tidal coupling to the core, potentially contributing to dynamo action.

repl.title: Gravitational-wave responses and noise correlations in geometric time-delay interferometry
repl.summary: Space-based gravitational-wave observations will probe the formation and growth of massive black holes and the evolution of compact binaries in the millihertz band. We develop a geometric-link representation of time-delay interferometry using six round-trip and six non-round-trip two-link blocks. Starting from the one-way Doppler response, we derive the elementary block responses and a dictionary that expresses 45 known second-generation combinations in terms of these blocks and residual one-way measurements. Representative Michelson and Relay observables admit compact forms, from which analytical sky-averaged tensor responses are obtained for a fixed, equal-arm constellation. We also derive the noise covariance of the blocks, retaining cross-spectra between blocks that share measurement streams. The resulting noise spectra agree with direct one-way assembly. We apply this formulation to a narrowband compact-binary signal in an equal-arm LISA instrument model. For the Relay example, neglecting the shared-link cross-spectrum changes the low-frequency noise scaling and overestimates the conditional Fisher uncertainties in amplitude or distance by factors of 10.71 at 1~mHz and 3.37 at 3~mHz.

repl.title: Exact 1D Nonlinear Solutions for Proton-Driven Plasma Wakefields
repl.summary: We extend the classical 1D nonlinear relativistic plasma wakefield paradigm to evaluate the pristine fluid profiles driven by intense relativistic proton trains under the comoving coordinate approximation. Using an intense two-bunch scheme, our adaptive integration model is validated down to machine precision against exact closed-form cold-fluid invariants, confirming that interface boundary corners represent physical step discontinuities in the second potential derivative. Scaling to an $N=100$ micro-bunch train, we resolve macroscopic phase-accumulation and subsequent nonlinear detuning by deriving a closed-form, parameter-free piecewise analytical envelope expression. This solution successfully maps the initial unattenuated quadratic coherent growth alongside the flat asymptotic horizontal saturation horizon governed by nonlinear energy conservation. Furthermore, the framework analytically evaluates the transient envelope overshoot, tracking its decay onto the saturation boundary via an exact phase-slip integration length scale. Providing immediate, ready macro-envelope bounds, this computationally inexpensive tool eliminates empirical adjustments and yields a robust mathematical baseline designed to guide and accelerate complex, multi-dimensional particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations through rapid parameter space exploration before deploying heavy computational assets. It establishes an efficient foundation to optimize asymmetric, custom-shaped driver profiles required to break the fundamental symmetric transformer ratio limit of 2 to make current particle accelerators more efficient.

repl.title: Entropic Chaplygin-Gas cosmology and late-universe tension diagnostics
repl.summary: We investigate an entropic generalized Chaplygin-gas (gCg) cosmology in which a single dark fluid accounts for both dark matter and dark energy. We constrain the model using DESI baryon acoustic oscillations, redshift-space-distortion measurements, compressed Planck 2018 distance and lensing information, and Type Ia supernova likelihoods with PantheonPlus+SH0ES (PPS) and DES--Dovekie. For Planck+DESI+RSD+PPS, the entropic gCg model yields a Hubble constant of $H_{0}=68.64\pm0.52\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ and the amplitude of matter fluctuations parameter of $S_{8}=0.797\pm0.021$, compared with $H_{0}=67.31\pm0.28\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ and $S_{8}=0.809\pm0.021$ in $\Lambda$CDM. The simultaneous upward shift in $H_{0}$ and downward shift in $S_{8}$ occurs in the directions required for a partial alleviation of both tensions. We also show that when PPS is replaced by DES--Dovekie, the parameter shifts are smaller, the best-fit improvement is negligible, and the Bayesian evidence favours $\Lambda$CDM. Thus, the entropic gCg model provides a potentially interesting simultaneous shift of the Hubble constant and the matter-clustering amplitude, but its statistical support depends on the adopted supernova likelihood.

repl.title: Penrose process in radiating Kerr-Vaidya black holes: efficiency, energy transport, and the viability boundary
repl.summary: We study single-particle Penrose extraction from a rotating black hole whose mass decreases in time, described by the ingoing Kerr-Vaidya metric, imposing exact four-momentum conservation at the decay. We prove that the local efficiency is bounded by the instantaneous Kerr value, through a covariant bound that reduces to the Bardeen-Press-Teukolsky limit at the horizon, and we derive an exact transport law, dE/dtau = -dm/dt (r/Sigma) p_r^2 for fixed spin parameter, by which every timelike geodesic gains energy while the hole loses mass. The net energy gain therefore splits into a local Penrose term and two transport terms, which we compute numerically as functions of spin and mass-loss rate for two mass-loss laws. With fixed spin parameter, extraction is possible only below a critical rate alpha_crit(a) = (M-a)/Delta v, set by the approach of the hole to extremality; with fixed a/m no such boundary exists. The transport law extends to the Kerr-Newman-Vaidya family, and the regime where the dynamics matter is shown to lie far outside astrophysical mass-loss rates.
